hints.title: String Transformation Minimum Operations Obstacle
hints.text: Converting word1 into word2 permits inserting, deleting, or replacing a character. How can evaluating prefix transformations determine the minimum edits between the full words?

hints.title: Three-Operation Minimum Invariant
hints.text: If word1[i - 1] == word2[j - 1], cost equals diagonal state. Otherwise, cost is 1 plus the minimum of replacement (diagonal), insertion (left), and deletion (above).

hints.title: 1D Rolling Row Operation Procedure
hints.text: Initialize a 1D array of size n + 1 with values 0 to n. For each character i in word1, set the first column to i and maintain the top-left diagonal value. For each character j in word2: if characters match, next value is diagonal; otherwise 1 + min(diagonal, left, above). Return the final entry.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Fills the Levenshtein distance table using a 1D buffer of length N + 1.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recursive branching across three choices takes O(3^max(M,N)) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Compresses M x N table into 1D row buffer of size N + 1.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Mapping insertion, deletion, and replacement to grid neighbor directions.
